{
  "reviews": [
    {
      "benchmark": "arc",
      "instrument_review": "ARC-AGI-2 evaluates AI performance on unfamiliar coloured-grid transformations inferred from examples. This review covers the public test problems, inspected official scoring software and ARC Prize verified-testing rules described in the supplied passage. Evidence supports a defined grid-task comparison; broader reasoning interpretations remain unresolved. The original EFPA 2025 model is retained, with explicit adaptations for AI assessment. Section ratings are judgements, not averages; no aggregate quality score is calculated.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "Part A, 1: Instrument name: ARC-AGI-2. Developers: ARC Prize Foundation staff and partners; individual authors and publisher roles are not fully identified. The example credits François Chollet and colleagues. Source inspection date: 7 October 2026; this is not an established publication or review date.",
        "2.1: Other—inferring grid-transformation rules. 2.2: Other—AI benchmarking and reasoning research. 2.3: Intended assessed population: AI systems solving unfamiliar grid problems; no narrower eligibility population is stated. 2.4: AI comparison is intended; user professions or qualifications are not specified.",
        "2.5: One reported task-performance score; no separately established skill scales. 2.6: Other—AI-produced output grids; human keyboard or mouse response modes are not established. 2.8: Verified evaluations specify settings, spending limits and one run; other routes may differ.",
        "2.9: Production-based grid answers and task success in a computer-generated environment. Two attempts are permitted per new input. 2.10: Coloured grids; the actual model-facing encoding is unspecified. 2.11: 1,000 development problems and three 120-problem test sets; inputs per problem vary, without a stated minimum, maximum or typical count.",
        "2.13: Running and marking software are described; exact required hardware and connectivity are not. 2.15: Public, semi-private and private test sets differ in access and were matched for human difficulty. ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-2 are separate versions; AI equivalence is not established.",
        "3.1: Digital scoring of AI outputs. 3.2: Credit requires an exact grid match within two attempts; input credits are averaged within problems, then problem scores are averaged. 3.3: Other—mean fractional problem credit, without standard-score interpretation.",
        "5.1: Public problems, running software, marking tests, development-report information and verified-testing policies are described. 5.2: Public digital materials and a dated change record are available. Public data use Apache 2.0; hidden-data rules address confidentiality and handling.",
        "General description: Worked input-output examples precede new grids. The benchmark targets inference of unfamiliar rules with little specialist knowledge. Human puzzle trials informed selection, but the reported 407 people and 515 sessions concern a larger pool than the final benchmark.",
        "6.1.1=2; 6.2.1=2: The intended rule-inference construct and design motivation are understandable, but a detailed theoretical account supporting broader intelligence interpretations is absent.",
        "6.1.3, 6.1.3.1=2, 6.1.3.2=2, 6.1.3.3=2: Newly written and unused earlier puzzles, human trials, developer review and removal of repeated rules provide an explained development process; detailed selection analyses remain unavailable.",
        "6.1.8=2: The passage supports an adequate rationale and development account for the narrow grid-task purpose; missing psychometric analyses prevent stronger judgement.",
        "6.2.2=2; 6.2.4=2: Development and verified-testing arrangements are described, including human trials, fixed evaluation conditions and one-run testing, without complete procedural detail.",
        "6.2.7=2: Content-development reasoning and duplicate-rule review provide some documented content evidence; reviewer expertise and agreement are not fully reported.",
        "6.2.11=2: Public exposure, hidden-data handling, recorded settings and limits on evaluation-specific tuning are discussed, providing some support for fair comparisons.",
        "6.2.13=2: The supplied account uses understandable, neutral language; this rating concerns the inspected passage, not all original documentation.",
        "6.2.14=2: Documentation adequately explains the narrow task and scoring, while uncertainty, broader validity and reporting remain incompletely documented.",
        "6.3.1=2; 6.3.2=2: Core administration and exact-match scoring rules are explained. Public marking tests check several error cases, although the whole scorer was not independently tested.",
        "6.3.4=2: The passage distinguishes fractional problem credit from fully solved problems and restricts broader interpretation.",
        "6.3.6=2; 6.3.7=2: Exposure risks, development versus evaluation use, and differing testing routes are identified; they provide limited but relevant comparison guidance.",
        "6.3.10=2; 6.4=2: An adequate procedural and documentation account supports narrow grid-task evaluation; this does not establish adequate reliability or broad validity.",
        "7.1, 7.1.2=2: The task's required operation is understandable from the supplied description: infer a transformation and return a complete output grid.",
        "10.1: Content evidence is considered under 6.1.3.2 and 6.2.7, as the original model directs. Human trials and developer review support task selection, without establishing general intelligence coverage.",
        "10.3.1.1: Other—human puzzle-performance comparisons with recorded background factors. 10.3.1.7=2: The reported absence of clear background relationships provides limited evidence concerning human puzzle accessibility; it does not validate AI-score interpretations.",
        "10.4.1: Other—design measures intended to discourage brute-force routes and repeated solution rules. 10.4.2=2; 10.4.3=2: These measures provide limited, relevant support for the intended interpretation, without excluding every unintended route.",
        "10.5=2: For the narrow interpretation of observed grid-task success, task content and exact-answer scoring provide adequate evidence. Broader reasoning, intelligence and real-world prediction are not established.",
        "11.1.1=2; 11.1.2=2: Low-specialist-knowledge design and documentation of exposure and testing conditions address some comparison concerns.",
        "11.3=2: Human piloting and background comparisons informed development; these findings cannot establish equivalence across AI systems.",
        "11.8=2: Some support exists for comparisons under verified conditions, particularly recorded settings and exposure controls. This judgement does not establish freedom from bias across systems."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "3.2, 6.3.2: Fractional software credit and the dataset's fully-solved terminology differ; reports must identify which outcome they mean.",
        "6.1.3.3, 7.1.7: Post-release fixes addressed coloured squares and unclear examples. This documents specific material problems and corrective work, not the prevalence of remaining errors.",
        "8.3.2.1, 9.4, 10.5: Corrected materials can change comparisons, and the change record does not recalculate every affected AI score.",
        "9.3, 9.7: Verified testing uses one run; human difficulty matching does not measure AI repeatability or sensitivity to presentation and software settings.",
        "11: Public evaluation problems permit prior exposure. Hidden-data agreements and monitoring reduce some risks, while the passage acknowledges possible leakage.",
        "Final evaluation: The strongest supported use is comparison on the specified grid tasks under recorded conditions. Different testing routes and broader intelligence claims require separate evidence."
      ],
      "missing_information": [
        "1: Reviewer identity, current review date, previous review date, local name or adaptation, named original authors, adaptation authors, local distributor, original publisher, current-edition publication date, local-adaptation publication date and original publication date are not established. No local adaptation is identified.",
        "2.4: Intended user qualifications are unstated. 2.12.1: Individual versus group administration is not explicitly classified. 2.12.2: Verified testing is controlled, but human proctoring, identity controls and correspondence to the original administration categories are incompletely specified.",
        "2.14: Preparation, administration, scoring, analysis and feedback times for administrators are unstated. Automated scoring is described, but complete automation is insufficiently specified to assign all relevant user times zero.",
        "2.16: Released sets contain specified problems; randomisation, ordering, adaptive selection and stopping rules for the reviewed administration are not fully described.",
        "3.4: No standard-score transformation is reported. 3.5: No differentiated norms are reported; this does not establish that no reference information exists elsewhere.",
        "4.1: Availability and number of digitally generated interpretive reports are unknown. 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7, 4.8, 4.9, 4.10: Report name, presentation, structure, context sensitivity, development, modifiability, transparency, content and intended recipients are not established. Published scores and outputs do not by themselves establish such a report.",
        "5.3: Supplier-required qualifications are unspecified; do not infer 'none'.",
        "6.1.2=0: No adequate summary of empirical construct research is supplied. 6.1.5: Psychometric framework not specified; quantitative per-item difficulty, discrimination, item-total, IRT, distractor and DIF indices are not supplied.",
        "6.1.6=0; 6.1.7=0: Human difficulty-informed selection is described, but item-analysis methodology and results are insufficient to assess psychometric item quality.",
        "6.2.6=0; 6.2.8=0; 6.2.9=0; 6.2.10=0: Detailed documentation of precision, dimensionality, AI-score relations with other variables, and systematic alternative validation studies is insufficient.",
        "6.2.12=0: Interpretive-report documentation is unavailable. 6.3.8=0: Hardware, software requirements, error recovery and support arrangements are insufficiently described. 6.3.9=0: Detailed supporting references and cross-references are not supplied.",
        "7.1.1=0; 7.1.3=0; 7.1.4=0; 7.1.5=0; 7.1.7=0; 7.1.8=0: The passage does not permit adequate evaluation of operational robustness, full instructions, response submission, interface design, item-content quality or overall digital materials. An example and marking tests do not establish these qualities.",
        "9.1: No AI reliability coefficients, measurement errors or subgroup precision estimates are provided.",
        "9.2.1=0; 9.2.2: No coefficients reported; 9.2.3=0; 9.2.4: No relevant sample-matching information. Internal consistency's suitability for the intended grid-task score is unresolved.",
        "9.3.1=0; 9.3.2=0; 9.3.3: No retest interval; 9.3.4: No relevant sample information. Repeated identical-condition AI evaluations are not supplied.",
        "9.4.1=0; 9.4.2=0; 9.4.3: No AI alternate-form sample information. Human-matched set difficulty does not establish AI-score equivalence.",
        "9.5.1=0; 9.5.2: No IRT precision indicators reported; 9.5.3=0. IRT use and its suitability are not established.",
        "9.7.1=0; 9.7.2: No systematic alternative precision method; 9.7.3=0. 9.8=0: AI-score precision cannot be rated from the supplied evidence.",
        "10.2.1: No dimensionality techniques supplied; 10.2.2=0; 10.2.3=0: Structure and invariance/DIF evidence for AI scores is unavailable.",
        "10.3.1.2=0; 10.3.1.3=0; 10.3.1.4=0; 10.3.1.5=0; 10.3.1.6=0: No justified AI-group hypotheses, convergent or discriminant correlations, MTMM results or quasi-experimental validation are supplied.",
        "10.3.1.8=0: The human study totals do not specify the relevant analysed samples or validate AI comparisons. 10.3.1.9=0: Marker quality is unestablished. 10.3.1.10: Study ages unknown. 10.3.1.11=0: Relations-to-other-variables evidence is insufficient for AI-score interpretation.",
        "10.3.2.1: No predictive, concurrent or postdictive external-criterion study established. 10.3.2.2=0; 10.3.2.3=0; 10.3.2.4=0; 10.3.2.6: Study ages unknown; 10.3.2.7=0. Prediction beyond grid tasks remains unresolved.",
        "11.2=0; 11.4=0; 11.5=0: Inclusive AI-facing design, precision across relevant system groups and validity equivalence are not systematically established.",
        "11.7=0: Report fairness cannot be assessed without report examples.",
        "12.1=0; 12.2=0; 12.3=0; 12.4=0; 12.5=0; 12.6=0; 12.7=0: Report scope, consistency, validity, fairness, acceptability, detail and overall adequacy cannot be rated. No report type or three scored profiles are supplied; report availability itself remains unknown.",
        "Final evaluation: Future development plans and ongoing research are not specified beyond continued corrections. Users need competence in benchmark administration, scoring and uncertainty; supplier qualification requirements are unknown."
      ],
      "reinterpretations": [
        "Rating key: n/a means inapplicable; 0 means insufficient evidence, not demonstrated inadequacy; 1 inadequate; 2 adequate; 3 good; 4 excellent. Original thresholds are not applied without appropriate coefficients, samples and intended-use information.",
        "2.7: Original human attention, language command, language fluency, digital skills, handedness, hearing, motor capabilities, reading, vision and writing questions are n/a as human capabilities. Adapted language, grid-input and output-format requirements have information missing; no additional prerequisite is established.",
        "2.17: The human-informant categories are n/a. Adapted informant: the assessed AI produces task responses; these are performance outputs, not psychological self-report.",
        "2.12, 2.13, 2.14: Administration categories, technology and timing refer to the evaluation operator and model execution. Human study session duration is not AI test duration.",
        "3.3, 3.4: Fractional task credit is not a percentile or standard score; standard-score transformation is n/a.",
        "6.1.4=n/a; 6.2.3=n/a: No translated or locally adapted version is identified. This review's AI reinterpretation is not evidence of a developer translation procedure.",
        "6.2.5=n/a; 6.3.3=n/a: No normative score interpretation is identified. 6.3.5=n/a for human-taker debriefing; guidance for communicating results to AI stakeholders remains unstated.",
        "7.1.6=n/a for human disability accessibility of an AI examinee. Model-interface compatibility is a relevant adapted question, but evidence is absent.",
        "7.2, 7.2.1=n/a, 7.2.2=n/a, 7.2.3=n/a, 7.2.4=n/a, 7.2.5=n/a, 7.2.6=n/a, 7.2.7=n/a: No paper-and-pencil or other physical AI administration is described.",
        "8, 8.1, 8.1.1=n/a, 8.1.2=n/a, 8.1.3, 8.1.3.1=n/a, 8.1.3.2=n/a, 8.1.3.3=n/a, 8.1.4=n/a: Narrow comparison of raw task scores does not require human population norms. Human puzzle trials are development evidence, not AI norms.",
        "8.2, 8.2.1, 8.2.1.1=n/a, 8.2.1.2=n/a, 8.2.1.3=n/a, 8.2.1.4=n/a, 8.2.1.5=n/a, 8.2.2=n/a: No competence cut score is claimed. Exact-answer keys are scoring rules, not expert-set or empirically validated competence thresholds.",
        "8.3, 8.3.1=n/a, 8.3.2=n/a, 8.3.2.1=n/a, 8.3.2.2=n/a, 8.3.2.3=n/a, 8.3.3=n/a: Norm age, adequacy, absence, fair use and overall norm quality are inapplicable to the narrow raw-score use. This exception cannot justify broader intelligence interpretations.",
        "9.6, 9.6.1=n/a, 9.6.2=n/a, 9.6.3=n/a: Exact-match scoring involves no judgemental response rating. Scorer correctness remains relevant under 6.3.2.",
        "10.3.2.5=n/a: No diagnostic classification purpose is stated; grid success is not diagnostic sensitivity or specificity.",
        "11: Human demographic fairness questions are not directly transferable to AI examinees. Adapted ratings concern relevant system groups, access, exposure and administration. Human background findings cannot establish AI fairness.",
        "11.6, 11.6.1=n/a, 11.6.2=n/a: Neither population-norm interpretation nor competence-cutoff interpretation is specified.",
        "Summary of Ratings: 6.4=2; 7.1.8=0; 7.2.7=n/a; 8.3.3=n/a; 9.8=0; 10.5=2 for narrow grid-task interpretation; 11.8=2; 12.7=0 pending report identification. No cross-section total is calculated.",
        "Final evaluation—critical qualities: Precision and validity for the claimed use are critical. Under EFPA's original 0/1 rule, precision=0 restricts decision-bearing use to research or exceptional expert use. This reflects insufficient evidence, not proof that scores are unreliable.",
        "Part C: Sources used only: the supplied ARC-AGI-2 passage and EFPA AISBL (2025), Test Review Model, version 5.0, https://www.efpa.eu/, CC BY-SA 4.0. This AI application is an explicitly adapted review and does not imply EFPA endorsement."
      ],
      "closing_note": "No numbered descriptive field or rated item is intentionally omitted; grouped IDs share the stated rationale. Unclear instructions concern fractional credit versus 'fully solved', model-facing formats and conditions outside verified testing. The EFPA summary references 7.2.8, while the supplied rated item is 7.2.7; no separate 7.2.8 is supplied."
    },
    {
      "benchmark": "designqa",
      "instrument_review": "DesignQA evaluates AI answers about Formula SAE rules, terminology and vehicle materials through six question groups. This review covers the original benchmark described in the 2024 paper and its public scoring software, as represented in the supplied passage. Scores describe task performance under the stated information-supply conditions; general engineering competence and fine rankings remain unresolved. The original EFPA 2025 model is retained with explicit AI reinterpretations. No aggregate quality score is calculated.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "Part A, 1: Instrument name and short name: DesignQA. Researchers and engineers created it; individual authors and publisher identities are not supplied. The original paper is dated 2024. Sources were inspected on 6 October 2026; that is not an established review or revision-publication date.",
        "2.1: Other—engineering-rule retrieval, document understanding and design checking. 2.2: Other—AI benchmarking on engineering-document tasks. 2.3: Intended assessed population: AI systems answering these questions. 2.4: AI comparison is intended; user professions and qualifications are unspecified.",
        "2.5: Six group scores and an equally weighted overall score. Groups concern individual rules, related rules, terminology, component presence, dimensions and functional performance; distinct underlying skills are not established.",
        "2.6: Other—AI-generated text or yes/no responses, sometimes with explanations. 2.8: Instructions and settings are described, but whole-rulebook versus retrieved-passage supply differs across systems.",
        "2.9: Open text answers and binary yes/no decisions; explanations may also be scored. 2.10: Written rules, images and drawings. 2.11: 1,451 question-answer pairs in six groups; individual-rule retrieval has 1,192 questions and functional performance has 16. Other group counts are not supplied.",
        "2.13: Public scoring software is described; required hardware and connectivity are not. 2.15: Passage-supply and visual-presentation variants are studied, without established parallel-form equivalence.",
        "3.1: Digital scoring of AI responses. 3.2: Methods include text similarity and correct yes/no decisions; explanations may receive text-similarity scores. The software weights the six groups equally. 3.3: Other—group-specific task metrics and an equal-weight composite.",
        "5.1: Public questions, instructions, scoring code, small marking-test files and some AI responses are available. 5.2: Public digital materials and code history are described.",
        "General description: DesignQA uses one competition rulebook, vehicle designs and test data to examine rule finding, terminology, drawing interpretation and compliance checking. Practitioners and researchers contributed, and additional reviewers checked many manually written questions.",
        "6.1.1=2; 6.2.1=2: The task rationale connects benchmark activities to parts of engineering work; it does not establish comprehensive engineering understanding.",
        "6.1.3, 6.1.3.1=2, 6.1.3.2=2, 6.1.3.3=2: Authentic materials, practitioner contributions and question review explain basic development decisions, although review exceptions and uneven coverage limit support.",
        "6.1.8=2: Adequate development rationale supports examination of these specific tasks; it does not establish a representative engineering assessment.",
        "6.2.2=2; 6.2.4=2: Question development, review, model instructions and settings are described, but full result-specific procedures are incompletely linked.",
        "6.2.7=2: Authentic sources and reviewer checks provide some documented content evidence; agreement and remaining error rates are not established.",
        "6.2.10=2: Documentation describes sensitivity to supplied passages, labels, scale bars and highlighting; these are relevant alternative sources of evidence.",
        "6.2.11=2: Unequal information supply, public exposure and formatting effects are discussed, giving users some comparison cautions.",
        "6.2.13=2: The supplied account is understandable and neutral; the quality of all original documentation is not established.",
        "6.2.14=2: Documentation adequately explains the narrow tasks and major limitations, while precision and reproducibility support remain incomplete.",
        "6.3.1=2; 6.3.2=2: Main administration and scoring approaches are explained, with small marking tests and discussion of scoring failures; complete accuracy checks are absent.",
        "6.3.4=2; 6.3.6=2; 6.3.7=2: The passage supports restricted interpretation by identifying differing information supplies, domain limits and uncertainty about small differences.",
        "6.3.10=2; 6.4=2: The supplied procedural and documentation account is adequate for understanding the narrow evaluation and its limitations.",
        "7.1, 7.1.2=2: Required task operations are understandable: answer questions using rules, images or drawings.",
        "10.1: Following the original model, content evidence is considered under 6.1.3.2 and 6.2.7. Real materials and engineering contributions support relevance within the sampled domain.",
        "10.3.1.1: Differences between tested AI systems and a random baseline are reported; these alone are not convergent or discriminant validation.",
        "10.4.1: Other—input and presentation perturbations addressing response processes and unintended influences. 10.4.2=2; 10.4.3=2: These provide limited evidence about task dependencies; one system's five passage sets do not establish identical-condition repeatability.",
        "10.5=2: The content and evaluation provide adequate support for examining performance on the specified tasks under stated input conditions. The composite is not established as a distinct competence measure.",
        "11.1.1=2; 11.1.2=2: Domain boundaries and several influences beyond engineering understanding are explicitly discussed.",
        "11.8=2: Documentation provides some support for cautious comparisons by revealing information-supply and scoring limitations; equivalent conditions and subgroup validity are not established."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "2.11, 6.1.3.1, 10.1: Question coverage is highly uneven: 1,192 individual-rule questions versus 16 functional-performance questions. One rulebook and limited task types restrict domain coverage.",
        "3.2, 6.3.2: Missing commas and valid related rules absent from reference answers can affect credit. These are documented scoring problems, not merely missing validation.",
        "3.2, 10.2: Equal weighting combines groups with different sizes and marking methods; the passage does not establish that this composite measures a distinct underlying skill.",
        "2.8, 11: Some systems receive the full rulebook and others retrieved passages. Scores therefore reflect the AI together with its information supply.",
        "9.7, 10.4: Changing passage sets provides variation evidence but does not isolate repeatability under identical conditions.",
        "10.4, 11.3: All described scale-bar drawings comply with the relevant rule, so always answering yes would earn their binary decision credit. The passage does not show that any tested AI used this route.",
        "5.1, 6.2.4: One released answer file contains fewer rows than the corresponding paper count. Exact historical code, settings and inputs are not fully linked to every result.",
        "Final evaluation: Small score differences deserve caution; in the 16-question performance group, one correct answer changes accuracy by the passage's stated 6.25 percentage points. Generalisation to other documents or real engineering projects is unestablished."
      ],
      "missing_information": [
        "1: Reviewer identity, current review date, previous review date, local version or adaptation, named original authors, adaptation authors, local distributor, original publisher, current-revision date and local-adaptation publication date are not supplied. The paper year does not establish an exact benchmark-release date.",
        "2.4: Intended user qualifications are unstated. 2.12.1: Individual versus group administration is not explicitly classified. 2.12.2: Supervision, identity controls and controlled-access arrangements are not fully specified.",
        "2.14: Administrator preparation, administration, scoring, analysis and feedback times are not supplied. Digital scoring alone does not establish complete zero-time automation.",
        "2.16: The benchmark has a published question collection, but exact ordering, selection, randomisation and any stopping rules for every reported result are not fully described.",
        "3.4: No standard-score transformation is reported. 3.5: No differentiated norms are reported.",
        "4.1: Availability and number of digitally generated interpretive reports are unknown. 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7, 4.8, 4.9, 4.10: Report identity, presentation, structure, context sensitivity, development, modifiability, transparency, content and recipients are not established. Paper results and AI answers are not automatically interpretive reports.",
        "5.3: Supplier-required qualifications are unspecified. A licence file and complete responsible-reuse rules were not found in the inspected materials; this does not establish prohibited reuse or unavailable permission.",
        "6.1.2=0: No adequate empirical construct-research summary is supplied. 6.1.5: Psychometric framework not specified; no systematic item difficulty, discrimination, item-total, IRT, distractor or DIF indices supplied.",
        "6.1.6=0; 6.1.7=0: Manual review is described, but sufficient psychometric item-analysis methods and results are not supplied.",
        "6.2.6=0; 6.2.8=0; 6.2.9=0: Detailed precision, dimensionality and external-relations validation documentation is insufficient.",
        "6.2.12=0: Interpretive-report documentation is unavailable. 6.3.8=0: Hardware, software compatibility, error handling and technical support are insufficiently specified. 6.3.9=0: Detailed supporting references and cross-references are not provided in the passage.",
        "7.1.1=0; 7.1.3=0; 7.1.4=0; 7.1.5=0; 7.1.7=0; 7.1.8=0: Robustness, complete instructions, response submission, interface quality, overall item-content quality and overall digital-material quality cannot be assessed adequately from the summary.",
        "9.1: No sufficient AI reliability coefficients, measurement errors or subgroup precision estimates are supplied.",
        "9.2.1=0; 9.2.2: No coefficients reported; 9.2.3=0; 9.2.4: Sample matching unknown. Suitability of internal consistency within each heterogeneous question group is not established.",
        "9.3.1=0; 9.3.2=0; 9.3.3: No identical-condition retest interval; 9.3.4: Relevant sample matching unknown. Repeated fixed-condition precision is not established.",
        "9.4.1=0; 9.4.2=0; 9.4.3: No relevant equivalence sample information. Input variants are not demonstrated equivalent alternate forms.",
        "9.5.1=0; 9.5.2: No IRT precision indicators; 9.5.3=0. IRT use and suitability are not established.",
        "9.6.1=0; 9.6.2: No agreement or reliability coefficients; 9.6.3=0 for judgement-dependent reference-answer review. Two additional reviewers are mentioned, with exceptions, but disagreement and residual errors are unknown.",
        "9.7.1=0; 9.7.2: Five passage sets for one AI provide limited variation evidence but no adequate identical-condition precision method; 9.7.3=0. 9.8=0: Precision needed to interpret close rankings cannot be rated adequately.",
        "10.2.1: No dimensionality techniques supplied; 10.2.2=0; 10.2.3=0: Six task labels and an overall score do not establish latent structure or invariance/DIF.",
        "10.3.1.2=0: Expected group differences lack sufficiently justified validation hypotheses. 10.3.1.3=0; 10.3.1.4=0; 10.3.1.5=0; 10.3.1.6=0; 10.3.1.7=0: Convergent, discriminant, MTMM, quasi-experimental construct validation and other external-variable evidence are insufficient. Input perturbations are addressed separately under 10.4.",
        "10.3.1.8=0: The 1,451 questions are not the number of assessed AI systems in an external-relations study. 10.3.1.9=0: Marker quality is unestablished. 10.3.1.10: Validation-study ages unknown. 10.3.1.11=0: External-variable validation remains insufficient.",
        "10.3.2.1: No established predictive, concurrent or postdictive study against independent engineering outcomes. 10.3.2.2=0; 10.3.2.3=0; 10.3.2.4=0; 10.3.2.6: Study ages unknown; 10.3.2.7=0. Real materials alone do not demonstrate criterion prediction.",
        "11.2=0; 11.3=0; 11.4=0; 11.5=0: Inclusive design, broad piloting, subgroup precision and validity equivalence across relevant AI conditions are not systematically established.",
        "11.7=0: Report fairness cannot be assessed without report examples.",
        "12.1=0; 12.2=0; 12.3=0; 12.4=0; 12.5=0; 12.6=0; 12.7=0: Report scope, consistency, validity, fairness, acceptability, detail and overall adequacy cannot be rated. No identified report type with three scored profiles is supplied; availability remains unknown.",
        "Final evaluation: No protected test set, systematic exposure check, sufficiently clear evaluation-training or repeated-submission rules, or human-engineer baseline is established. These absences do not alone demonstrate poor performance or invalidity.",
        "Final evaluation: Ongoing research and future development plans are not specified. Users need engineering-domain, administration and scoring competence; consistency with supplier qualification requirements is unknown."
      ],
      "reinterpretations": [
        "Rating key: n/a means inapplicable; 0 means insufficient evidence, not demonstrated inadequacy; 1 inadequate; 2 adequate; 3 good; 4 excellent. Original numerical guides require suitable evidence and are not mechanically transferred to AI accuracy or text-similarity metrics.",
        "2.7: Original human attention, language command, language fluency, digital skills, handedness, hearing, motor capabilities, reading, vision and writing questions are n/a as human capabilities. Adapted requirements include processing supplied technical text or images and producing required answers; minimum compatibility and prerequisite levels have information missing. No additional requirement is established.",
        "2.17: Human-informant categories are n/a. Adapted informant: the assessed AI supplies performance responses, rather than psychological self-report.",
        "2.12, 2.13, 2.14: Administration, technology and timing concern model execution and evaluation operators; public availability does not establish a human Internet-testing category.",
        "3.3, 3.4: Accuracy and similarity metrics are task scores, not population-standardised scores; standard-score transformation is n/a.",
